data.name: Chahrazad
data.gender_notes: Chahrazad is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: She who has many stories or tales. In Arabic folklore, Scheherazade is a legendary storyteller who delays her husband's plans to kill her by telling him a new story each night. The name Chahrazad carries the meaning “Storyteller” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Chahrazad usually hope their child will grow to embody storyteller and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Chahrazad belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Storyteller.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chahrazad total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Scheherazade is a significant figure in Middle Eastern and Islamic cultures, as she is known for her storytelling abilities and her innovative tales that have captivated generations. Her stories, collected in the book "One Thousand and One Nights," have deeply influenced literature, art, and entertainment throughout the Islamic world and beyond.
data.spiritual_significance: Scheherazade's story represents the power of storytelling, creativity, and imagination in connecting people from different cultures, beliefs, and backgrounds. It serves as a reminder of the importance of using language and art to bridge divides, foster understanding, and create meaningful relationships. Additionally, it highlights the role of women as storytellers and culture bearers in Islamic civilization.
